rationale: A wins because it keeps the real stories separated and shows its receipts. "Airtable retires its 'spreadsheet-database' pitch for an 'AI-native app platform' one" is a clean category angle, and the caveat "not proof it's already an industry-wide move" is exactly the kind of adult supervision this work needs. B is useful, but "pre-AI decacorns rebrand to survive" smuggles in a canned trend the fact block did not supply, and "Airtable's new agents read company records and act on them" is too close to the announcement wearing a category hat.
gaps_in_A: "employees are the ones left to catch what they get wrong" overstates the facts. The update says reliability data is not disclosed; it does not say employees carry the error burden or that there is no approval layer.

"the prevailing belief this cuts against: that enterprise AI agents are now trustworthy enough to act autonomously on production data" is a little too conveniently manufactured. A contrarian angle needs a real named belief in the market, not a straw version of launch hype.

"All four angles are blocked on the same gaps - reliability data, a valuation timeline, and a named customer or on-record exec quote" is overbroad. Reliability data blocks the governance angle; it does not equally block the category-positioning or valuation story.
gaps_in_B: "pre-AI decacorns rebrand to survive" is the big reach. The update gives Airtable's valuation context and repositioning, not a proven survival trend among decacorns.

"formally retiring the 'spreadsheet-database' identity it was built on" sharpens the facts past what was supplied. The update says Airtable is shifting messaging; it does not prove formal retirement or historical identity claims.

"Airtable's new agents read company records and act on them - updating statuses and drafting emails" is mostly a rewrite of the announcement. Calling it category-creation does not make it a category story.

"angles one and two are pitchable from the facts on file" is too breezy. Angle two still needs demo detail, permission model, pricing direction, and ideally a customer before a serious trade reporter does more than rewrite the launch.
